text: Started writing these down because Dev said I keep forgetting what I was worried about a month ago. Right now the Lantern beta is late and I feel like I'm the bottleneck.
Ran 5k for the first time since the injury. Slow, but it felt like getting something back.
Ana called. She's moving to Lisbon in the fall. I'm happy for her and also weirdly sad. We've never lived more than an hour apart.
Three days stuck on the sync bug and I'd decided I wasn't good enough for this job. Tonight it turned out to be clock skew and I fixed it in twenty minutes. Note to self: the stuck feeling lies.
Said yes to helping Priya with her app on top of everything else. Already regretting it.
Dad's knee surgery went fine. I drove him home and we talked more than we have in years.
I want to get better at saying no. Every time I take on something new, the thing I actually care about slips.
Bad week. Barely slept, skipped every run, snapped at Dev over nothing. Everything feels heavy and I just want to hide.
A little better. Walked with Ana on Sunday and it helped more than I expected. Talking to people helps. Hiding doesn't.
The Lantern beta finally went out to 40 people. Twelve replied the first day. One said it changed how she plans her week. In March I didn't think this would happen.
Thinking about quitting the day job eventually. Not yet. I need six months of runway first. I keep saying that and I mean it.
Ran three times this week. When I run I'm nicer to everyone, including myself.
I want fewer commitments, not more. Next quarter is about finishing Lantern and nothing else.
Ana left for Lisbon. The airport goodbye was rough. We set up a Sunday call.
That's not true: I don't hate my job, I hate the commute.
Missed the Sunday call with Ana because I was heads-down on the launch. Felt awful about it.
Hold me to this: no new projects until the Lantern launch is out.
Hold me to this: run three times a week, even in launch month.
Launch is set for October 20. I'm nervous, but it's the good kind.
Haven't run in ten days. Telling myself it's fine because of the launch.
Dev thinks I'm avoiding the pricing decision. He might be right.
Lantern pricing: leaning toward eight dollars a month. I keep second-guessing it.
